column1: # Arabic-script explicit terms — page-text scoring tier.
# Format:  term<TAB>weight     (see terms.en.tsv for what the weights mean)
# Terms are normalised at compile time by `terms.normalize()`, so write them
# however is natural: hamza forms (أ إ آ ٱ), alef maqsura (ى), taa marbuta (ة),
# tashkeel and tatweel are all folded away. `إباحية` and `اباحيه` compile to the
# same entry, and either spelling on a page matches it.
# Modern Standard Arabic is what a filter written from a dictionary covers, and
# it is almost never what adult content is actually written in. The material a
# user meets is in Egyptian (the dialect of most consumed media), Levantine,
# Gulf or Maghrebi — and those share very little explicit vocabulary. An
# MSA-only list looks comprehensive and catches a small fraction of real pages.
# Sections below are additive: a term listed under one dialect is often
# understood across several, so do not remove a duplicate just because it also
# appears elsewhere — the compiler dedupes by normalised form anyway.
# Arabic glues the definite article and prepositions onto the following word, so
# matching strips a BOUNDED set of affixes — and that stripping is exactly what
# makes short roots dangerous. `جنس` (sex) is a substring of `الجنسية`
# (nationality): matched carelessly, this list blocks every passport and visa
#   1. Short ambiguous roots get a LOW weight, never enough to block alone.
#   2. `negatives.tsv` carries the innocent words containing them, weighted
#      strongly enough to cancel the root.
# `زنا` is fiqh and criminal-law vocabulary before it is anything else, and
# it is a poor pornography signal: adult sites advertise with سكس and نيك,
# not with the legal term. At 6.0 it blocked a four-line islamqa fatwa
# titled `ما حكم الزنا؟` outright (score 77 against a threshold of 7.5).
